header: The DSP story card: how the Durgapur Steel Plant came to be, in five tabs. 1 "Story": the five dates, the plant in a few facts, and the whole timeline from 1954 to today, with SAIL's photographs and the source of every entry. 2 "Who made it": the idea (Nehru), the British technology, Dr B C Roy, Pandit Nehru, the Queen's visit, the President, the site and the city. 3 "First products": what the plant made at the very start, and what nobody wrote down. 4 "Heads of DSP": the chronological list of the heads, by the title each bore (General Manager, Director-in-Charge, Managing Director, CEO, Director In-charge), with a picture where SAIL has one. 5 "SAIL & units": the foundation of Hindustan Steel and of SAIL, its plants (with the country each came from) and its other bodies. All of it comes from a reviewed file with its sources (history.ts), and I fetch nothing. Where two sources differ I show both; where nothing is known the card says so.

symbols.name: LINK
doc: The one look of every link on this card (document names, page numbers, picture credits): I want it at rest to read as plain text of the surrounding colour (no underline, no colour); on hover ONLY its colour changes (the app's global rule, globals.css, a:hover, turns it blue; no underline), which is what tells the reader it is a link

symbols.name: Bold
doc: A note written with **two stars** round a phrase shows that phrase in bold; I read nothing else as markup.

symbols.name: BasisChip
doc: The chip beside a head's name ("SAIL record", "Memoir"...): it looks as it always did and says what the entry rests on; a click (or Enter) opens that source at its place. I made it a span with the role of a link, not an anchor or a button, so that the page's hover colour rule does not repaint it: only the pointer becomes a hand.

symbols.name: STACKED_UNDER
doc: These units share ONE cell of the two-column grid, the second under the first: I put a short card (Chandrapur) under a card that would otherwise stand in a row beside a much taller one (Visvesvaraya), so the pair ends exactly where the tall card ends instead of leaving a gap in one card and a lonely card below. The first keeps its own height; the second stretches to fill what is left (the cell is as tall as the taller neighbour).

symbols.name: DspHistoryCard
symbols.sig: export function DspHistoryCard({ initialTab = "story" }: { initialTab?: DspHistoryTab })
doc: `initialTab` is the tab the search line asked for: I open Heads for "dsp heads" and Who made it for "queen elizabeth durgapur".

behaviours: the card opens on the story tab with five tabs: The story, Who made it, First products, Heads of DSP, SAIL & units
the five key dates are drawn (October 1956, January 1957, December 26, 1959, April 24, 1960, January 24, 1973) and the eight facts, each with its source
the timeline has all 21 entries, each dated and sourced; eleven have SAIL's photograph (the Queen's visit has two, twelve pictures in all)
the Queen's visit, Nehru at the Section Mill and the Wheel Plant, Dr Roy at the Merchant Mill and the President at the blast furnace are in it with their dates
where the sources differ the card says so (a note on the Coates mission, the blast furnace, the Merchant Mill, Shastri's title) and there is no picture-filter button (the owner removed it)
seven parts: the idea, Britain, Dr Roy, Nehru, the Queen, the President, the site
the Queen's night at 'Rani Kuthi' (Suite No. 1), the helicopter from Panagarh, Swaran Singh, and that the exact day is not in the sources
Dr Roy's and Nehru's pictures are shown (Merchant Mill 1962; Section Mill 1961 and Wheel Plant 1962) and the Queen's two (with Mr Niyogi; at the Durgapur Club)
Britain's part: Sir Eric Coates, ISCON of 13 companies, the contract of October 1956; the Niyogi of the site and the General Manager are kept apart

five first items from iron to the Wheel and Axle Plant, each with its date and its sources; the Merchant Mill's item says what it first rolled is NOT stated, and shows the 1961-or-1962 difference; no item is called bars or rounds
the memoir's list of early products is shown apart, in its own words, as a recollection, with the caution that the card does not list bars, rounds, billets or blooms among the first products

a cited page of a PDF is a link into the card's own viewer at THAT page (our route, #page=<the PDF page>, which is also what the link carries), not the top of the book; Steel Cities' printed p. 65 opens PDF page 33 (the book prints two pages to a sheet)
the card says the page numbers of Steel Cities are the printed ones, at the bottom of each page, and each page link carries the PDF page and the printed pages it holds as its tooltip
web pages are linked to the sentence cited (a text fragment), and every source cited at a page or a sentence has its words under "What it says"

the plant's JO manuals are named by their file (089, 086) and carry their page and words; only the page numbers are links, to OUR route (signed-in readers only), never to a web address of the manual, and the card says the page number opens it
the annual reports open the PDF page, not the printed one (SAIL 2022-23 printed p. 53 is PDF page 55; SAIL 2025-26 printed p. 49 is PDF page 51)
the five key dates carry their sources, on the card and behind the strip
what nobody wrote down is said: DSP's own tonnes for 1959-62 are in no source; Hindustan Steel's 0.158 MT and 1.6 MT are given as all the plants together
five eras with their titles and every listed head in order, from K K Sen to Surajit Mishra

eleven of them have a picture (five SAIL's: Sen, Niyogi, Bell, Wadhera, Mishra; six supplied: Bajaj, P K Singh, Rath, Dasgupta, Kamlakar, B P Singh) and eight show initials; the card says which are which

each head says on what its entry rests: SAIL record, SAIL report, Annual report, Press report, Obituary, Company report or Memoir (four from the memoir), and there is no strip of notes about it (the chip says it)
the Heads page opens with a short invitation to read the memoir (its author named, a link to the memoir itself, nothing else added to the intro)
the memoir link in the Heads intro is underlined (a clue among much text) and keeps the card's one link class otherwise

every list of sources shows ONE source, the first (the first head, Karunaketan Sen, shows SAIL's History Tree caption and nothing else), EXCEPT where the sources of an entry disagree: there the first and the other side are given, so a reader can open both

the Land fact shows both sides of its dispute: the book's 32 sq km (Steel Cities, p. 70, opening its PDF page 36) and SAIL's plant page, which says 40 sq km (a link to that sentence); only the first line has 'What it says', the others are opened to be read
a dispute over a date shows both sides: the Merchant Mill's first-products entry lists the plant manual (1961), SAIL's photograph and the Ministry's backgrounder (January 1962), each linked
in the first head's note the words 'ICS officer' are bold (the stars that mark them are not shown), and no other note shows stray stars

a source cited at page numbers has its NAME as plain text and only the page numbers as links (the JO Manuals, Steel Cities, the annual reports); a source with no page number keeps its name as the link (the History Tree)
the Heads page has no strip of notes on the sources or on spellings, and the card (a reading card with nothing to type into) carries no privacy and approximation notice
the gaps are drawn as gaps (five) and none is filled with a name
the dated heads: P K Bajaj from November 1, 2009, P K Singh May 2012 to December 2015, A K Rath March 2016, B P Singh April 19, 2022, Surajit Mishra July 15, 2025
the foundation of SAIL (Hindustan Steel January 19, 1954; SAIL January 24, 1973) and nine units, Durgapur marked 'this plant'
the country each plant came from: Britain (DSP), Germany (RSP), the USSR (BSP and BSL)

no pale strip round a picture (the Queen's picture showed a thin white line at its right edge: a 1 px pale border on a half pixel): the frame has no border; the picture reaches its edge, is laid one pixel larger than its frame on every side (the frame clips it), and a faint dark ring is drawn INSIDE its edge

every plant's short form stands in brackets to the right of its full name, as SAIL prints it: Bhilai Steel Plant (BSP), Rourkela Steel Plant (RSP), Durgapur Steel Plant (DSP), Bokaro Steel Plant (BSL), IISCO Steel Plant (ISP), Alloy Steels Plant (ASP), Salem Steel Plant (SSP), Visvesvaraya Iron and Steel Plant (VISL), Chandrapur Ferro Alloy Plant (CFP)
the town is shown with the state where the name leaves it out (Burnpur, Durgapur, Bhadravati), and the manual's other spelling of Visvesvaraya's short form (VISL) is said

the Visvesvaraya plant is drawn as Visvesvaraya Iron and Steel Plant (VISL) with 'SAIL also writes VISP', and the three units under disinvestment carry a 'Where it stands now' band with ONE source each, opened at its page or linked to its sentence

each of SAIL's other bodies shows its place beside its name (Central Marketing Organisation (CMO) in Kolkata, West Bengal; the Management Training Institute at Ranchi, Jharkhand; SAILCON in New Delhi), eight of the nine with a short form
no stray closing bracket: the sources of a body are a list under it, not wrapped in brackets (a bracket after the 'What it says' toggle stood alone on a line)
each head carries its sequence number, 1 to 19 in list order, in a round black badge with a gold ring and gold figures (one per row, none repeated, none skipped, the last is Surajit Mishra's)

each head's tenure stands in brackets right after its name (19 of them); the years in it are only years of the head's own dates; each is (start – end) with "not known" on the side no source gives; the five with both ends are Shyam Bahadur Singh (1993 – 2001), Bhattacharyya, P K Singh, B P Singh and the 2025 interim; Mishra is open at the end (present)
the story tab shows the Queen's visit with BOTH pictures, the one with Mr Niyogi first and the one at the Durgapur Club under it, inside the same event

every link on the card looks the same: plain text at rest (no underline, no blue); on hover only the colour changes (the global a:hover turns it blue), never an underline (the one exception, the memoir link in the Heads intro, is underlined at rest to show it is a link among much text); document names and page numbers share one class, and no tab draws a link underlined or coloured at rest

a picture has its caption and date and NO credit line or credit link under it (the owner's rule: a link is only under Source): no 'Photograph:' and no data-credit-link on any tab, each head's picture line is just 'Picture: caption (date).', and the story tab still has its 12 captioned pictures

each chip beside a head's name (19) is a link to its source and looks exactly as before: the same span and classes (rounded pill, 11px bold, its colour), only the hand cursor added; a span with the role of a link, so that the page's hover colour rule (it repaints a and button) does not change it; it can be reached and opened with the keyboard
the line at the foot of the card names the plant, not SAIL: "Durgapur Steel Plant (DSP) history, with its photographs · saved, not live"
the missing Managing Directors before Shyam Bahadur Singh are marked as missing, in a thick amber dashed box, between P K Paul and Shyam Bahadur Singh, and no name is put in their place

on the heads tab a head's picture stands at the TOP LEFT of its row, not at the middle of the text (a button centres its content: the button is self-start), 4 px down so that its top edge is level with the top of the visible letters of the name (measured on the rendered page: the picture's first dark row and the text's first dark row are the same pixel row)

Salem and Chandrapur share ONE cell of the grid, Chandrapur under Salem (measured in a browser: Salem keeps its own height with no empty space; Chandrapur fills what is left and ends exactly where the Visvesvaraya card on the right ends, at 1400, 1280, 1100 and 1024 px); the other seven plants stand alone; all nine cards are still there

SAIL's other bodies show their short forms to the right of the full names: Central Marketing Organisation (CMO), Management Training Institute (MTI), Centre for Engineering & Technology (CET), Research & Development Centre for Iron & Steel (RDCIS), SAIL Safety Organisation (SSO), SAIL Refractory Unit (SRU), SAIL Consultancy Division (SAILCON), Central Coal Supply Organisation (CCSO)
SAIL's other bodies are listed with their manual pages
every picture on the card is a file that exists (the paths are /dsp-history/...)
every picture has alt text
no tab has a question-mark badge or Bengali letters, no 'lakh', no 'Mt'
the card uses only the text sizes that have a rule in the search window's stylesheet (xs to 4xl and 9, 10, 11, 13, 15, 17, 28 px) and no fixed leading
the card has colour (gradients on the key dates, the eras and the units): it is not black and white
'dsp history', 'history of dsp', 'durgapur steel plant history', 'dsp story' open the story tab

'about dsp' (and 'About DSP?', 'about durgapur steel plant', 'about the durgapur steel plant', 'tell me about dsp') opens the whole card on its first tab, with all five tabs; 'about dsp phone numbers' and 'about sail' do not
'heads of dsp', 'dsp heads', 'former heads of dsp', 'dsp chief executives', 'dsp general managers', 'heads of durgapur steel plant' open the heads tab
'queen elizabeth durgapur', 'nehru durgapur', 'bc roy durgapur', 'who built dsp', 'dsp foundation' open the who-made-it tab; 'dsp first products' the first-products tab
'sail history', 'history of sail', 'sail foundation', 'foundation of sail', 'sail units' open the SAIL tab
other lines are not this card: 'dsp', 'history', 'queen', 'nehru', 'who is the head of dsp', 'head of dsp', 'dsp ceo', 'durgapur pin code', 'steel prices', 'sail steel', 'dsp products'
readLang reads the tab and falls back to the story
the timeline dots sit exactly on the line: the 12px dot is 23px left of its entry (2px line, 16px padding: 18 - 1 + 6 = 23), measured 0.000px off in a browser at 1x, 2x and 3x
